name: Portuguese Africa
alt: African possessions of the Portuguese Empire

predecessors.name: Portuguese Empire
predecessors.text: the Moroccan, Gold Coast, Cape Verde and Sao Tome patches of the Portuguese Empire's 1502-1506 shape, which Cliopatria moves to its own Portuguese Africa row in 1507

successors.name: Spanish Empire
successors.text: all 99 cells of the 1579 shape reappear in Cliopatria's Spanish Empire row from 1582

ledger.x: 1507: the African possessions of the Portuguese Empire become a row of their own.
1534: Cliopatria's shape adds twelve cells (Inhambane, the Zambezi-delta coast, two on the Gold Coast).

1541: the Portuguese give up Safi and Azemmour (and lose Agadir) to the Saadis. the page has the Portuguese abandoning Safi in 1541 after Saadi offensives and Azemmour in 1541 too, and Agadir was captured by the Saadis in 1541 under Mohammed ash-Sheikh.
1550: Alcacer-Ceguer (Ksar es-Seghir) and Arzila (Asilah) are abandoned.
1564: Cliopatria's shape adds six cells on the Cacheu coast of Guinea.
1576: Paulo Dias de Novais founds Luanda. the page has Paulo Dias de Novais establishing Luanda in 1576, soon a slave port; the Evolution page has Angola a colony from 1575.
1581: the Cortes of Tomar crown Philip II of Spain as Philip I of Portugal, who promised, the page says, to keep the empires legally distinct.

wars.name: Moroccan-Portuguese conflicts
wars.outcome: The Portuguese hold the Atlantic enclaves until the Saadi offensives of 1541 take Agadir and force the abandonment of Safi and Azemmour; Alcacer-Ceguer and Arzila follow in 1549-1550.

wars.name: Battle of Alcácer Quibir
wars.outcome: 4 August 1578 at Ksar-el-Kebir: Moroccan forces destroy the Portuguese army and King Sebastian is killed; the defeat leads to the succession crisis of 1580 and the union with Spain.

wars.name: Ndongo warfare after the Kabasa massacre
wars.outcome: In 1579 the Ndongo ruler massacred Portuguese and Kongolese residents at Kabasa; warfare with Ndongo continued for decades.

certainty.note: Every holding is a fort or town enclave (the Moroccan coast, Elmina, Cape Verde, Mozambique Island, Sofala, Luanda) whose hinterland no page defines; the Mozambique captaincy had no surveyed extent and the Moroccan enclave limits are the…
